summary: Essex County, VT lookout in Guildhall, under construction from 1922 and staffed in the 1940s and 1970s; FFLA lists the original and its West Topsham relocation as gone.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the Stone Mountain tower as Tower Gone and the West Topsham relocation as a radio tower, also Gone. The sources read give no date or site description for either.

events.note: August 1922 newspaper: construction started on a new tower on Stone Mountain in Guildhall; completion not described
New lookout cabin begun, with log lean-to, fireplaces and tables; old cabin moved for wood storage (report for the term ending June 30, 1938)
1948 Essex County Herald: a man employed at the fire tower; his family spent the summer at Stone Mountain
Tower ventilator replaced with a weatherproof cap (biennial report covering 1949-50)
May 1971 newspaper: a woman stationed on Stone Mountain was to be in charge of the fire tower
FFLA lists the original Stone Mountain tower as Tower Gone; no date given
FFLA lists a relocated Stone Mountain site at West Topsham, Orange County, as a Radio Tower, Gone; no date or mover in sources

notes_for_editor: The history (1922 construction, 1938 cabin, 1948 and 1971 staffing) rests on one Forest Lookouts page that quotes newspapers and state reports. Fate and present condition rest on one directory list, which gives a single line for each site. The brief's status 'relocated' is not wrong as a history, but the directory lists both the original and the West Topsham site as gone; facts.status is set to 'gone' for the editor to review. The brief's source page '../us-vt-stone-mountain-at-west-topsham/' has no research or story in the tree, so no child record was checked. A search snippet describes a station on Stone Mountain in the early 1920s (NorthWoods Stewardship Center), but the page returned HTTP 403, so it is not cited. Forest Lookouts' NGS block for PID PF1011 has no status line we could read; the word 'Removed' appears above it with no context, so it is not used. No photos found.
